The strengthened native 19-case candidate terminated with SIGSEGV after four passing cases. The Meson record contains no fault stack or diagnostic establishing its cause. This is an actual red run with stable source and executable identities; attribution and repair remain pending, and its final-named label does not make it acceptance. Later source review established that this fixture directly emitted show on an already visible popover, bypassing GTK native-show guards. It was replaced with native synchronous hide/reopen; that fixture mismatch alone does not pinpoint the native crashing statement. A later instrumented reproduction captured GTK offset 0x260359 during Fixture destruction. Matching disassembly to GTK source supports a leftover previous-focus unmap handler with stale popover userdata after synthetic show overwrites the tracked handler pair; that private callback identity is inferred, not resolved through debug symbols.

This private symbol identification is source/disassembly inference.
